### Introduction

The objective of this article
is to define
the Yang Mills action, as written in Section 3 @Chatterjee2016, 
omitting details along the 
way which I am comfortable ignoring.

Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, with 
the case of interest being $G = \UN$.
The Yang Mills action $S$ gives 
a number for each input of a $G$
connection form. 

The formula is
$$
\begin{equation}
    S(A) = \int_{\R^d} \Tr (F \wedge *F).
\end{equation}
$${#eq-YangMillsaction}
In this formula, $A$ is a $G$ connection 
form on $\R^d$. Meanwhile
$F$ is the curvature form of $A$. And
$*$ is the Hodge star operator.
These notions
of curvature, Hodge star operator, 
and Lie group connection forms
are buried deeply inside usual courses 
in geometry, so this article has 
its work cut out for itself.

### Means/Media

I will use LLMs (and remark where in the article they are being used),
pdfs of textbooks (with citations), pen and paper to work
out details myself, and video to present the article 
in a digital and verbal manner. This article is delivered via 
Quarto.

### Step one: Locating the correct notions in the textbook literature.

The first challenge is to locate
the desired notions of connection form, curvature, 
and Hodge star operator in 
the mathematics or physics literature.
We begin with the task of locating
the notion of Lie group connection
forms.
